The fix lies outside this task's FILES either way, which is why the actor is `plan`.

The confinement fence opens when `files` is omitted: `makeConfineHook` at factory/worker.mjs:51 sets `allowed = null` unless `files` is an array, and line 58 then computes `unlisted` as `false`, so a dispatch called without `files` permits every `Edit`/`Write`/`MultiEdit`/`NotebookEdit` anywhere inside `cwd`. M3 reads "not in `files`", which on an absent list denies everything rather than allowing everything. This is faithful to the prototype the Context names as the shape (`factory/proto/loop.mjs`'s `files && !files.includes(rel)`), and M1's signature always carries `files`, so it is advisory — but it is a fence whose failure mode on a missing argument is to open rather than close. Consider `const allowed = new Set((files ?? []).map(...))` so an omitted `files` denies every edit.

Readiness gates on `done`, not on adoption. In `runEngine`'s loop the id is added to `done` before `foldIn` runs, and a fold that parks only adds to `parked` — so `ready = tasks.filter(... waitsOn(t).every((d) => done.has(d)))` treats a PARKED dependency as satisfied. M1 says a task is dispatched "once every task it `depends_on` is adopted". Consequence on the fixture: if task 1's fold parked, task 2 (which consumes `make_widget` from it via `dag_edges`) would still be cloned and implemented against a head that never received task 1. The engine already has the right behaviour for this case — the `!ready.length` branch parks the remainder with a reason — it is simply unreachable while `done` doubles as the adoption set. No Proof leg exercises parking, so this is advisory, not a block.

The `factoryTools` consumption is structurally correct but functionally inert on the `--kata-url` path. `land` calls `tools({ task: { id, uid: task.uid, files }, candidates: [] })`: `compile_plan.py` emits no `uid` anywhere in `launch_waves` (grep for `uid` in the compiler returns nothing), so `task.uid` is always `undefined` and `factory/tools.mjs`'s `note`/`hand` would call `kata.comment(projectId, undefined, …)` / `kata.patchMetadata(projectId, undefined, …)`

and `candidates` is hard-coded `[]`, which `factory/tools.mjs:116` turns into a name list that rejects every `settled` symbol with "(none — the patch added no export)". M4 only requires that `factory/tools.mjs` be reached when `--kata-url` is given, and leg (d) reads only `typeof tools`, so nothing here is red — but the kata seam cannot actually work as wired. Either compute the candidate symbol names off the captured patch before constructing the server, or drop the two keys and say in a comment that the kata tools are unreachable until a uid source exists.
